papers.title_en: TerraAgent: Demonstration-Grounded Multi-Agent Reasoning for Long-Context Remote Sensing Visual Question Answering
papers.authors: Jingwen Huang, Yiming Fang, Hanxiao Wu, Boyuan He, Keyi Luo
papers.evidence: 面向长上下文遥感视觉问答的多智能体推理
papers.tldr: 遥感视觉问答需答案真正依赖图像，但现有RS MLLM仅看准确率，无法识别先验答题；跨域演示匹配差，长上下文稀释证据并传播误差。论文提出TerraAgent/AVA训练-free框架：GDR检索过滤演示，MACE分解证据DAG并路由工具，CVA反事实审计并算视觉依赖分。在RSVQA-LR/HR、VRSBench、LHRS-Bench上，准确率最高+2.40分，视觉依赖0.28→0.49，先验答题46.2%→21.7%，幻觉17.1%→9.8%，成本2.6倍且免微调。
papers.abstract_en: Remote sensing visual question answering (RS-VQA) requires answers that truly depend on image evidence, yet current remote sensing multimodal large language models (RS MLLMs) are still evaluated mainly by accuracy, which cannot reveal whether a correct answer was produced without using the image. This setting introduces three challenges: demonstrations retrieved across different ground sample distances (GSD), sensors, and city textures may be poorly matched; real queries often involve long visual contexts from multi-scale tiles, multi-temporal frames, and retrieved knowledge, where evidence can be diluted and errors can propagate through multi-step reasoning; and prior-only answering remains invisible to standard metrics. We present AVA, a training-free framework that wraps a frozen RS MLLM with three modules. GDR performs GSD-bucketed, scene-graph-based demonstration retrieval and filters demonstrations whose answers are unsupported by their images. MACE decomposes each query into an evidence-typed sub-question DAG, routes sub-questions to suitable perception tools, and records verified provenance in a shared evidence ledger with bounded re-perception. CVA audits the final answer through counterfactual perturbations of cited evidence, including ablation and swap, and computes a visual-dependency score for confidence calibration and evidence-forcing re-query. On RSVQA-LR/HR, VRSBench, and LHRS-Bench, AVA improves average accuracy by up to 2.40 points over the strongest same-setting baselines, raises the visual-dependency score from 0.28 to 0.49, reduces the prior-only answer rate from 46.2 percent to 21.7 percent, and lowers the hallucination rate from 17.1 percent to 9.8 percent, with 2.6x the cost of a single backbone forward pass and no fine-tuning.

papers.title_en: Knowing Whether, Not Just Where: Anchor-Probing Distillation for Open-Set Remote Sensing Visual Grounding
papers.authors: Zhihao Chang, Lei Zhai, Shuyuan Yang, Zhixi Feng
papers.evidence: 融合文本查询与影像的遥感视觉定位
papers.tldr: 遥感开放集视觉定位不仅要定位目标，还要判断图像是否提供足够证据。APD将开放集定位重构为视觉支持学习，用教师模型以原始查询为参考锚点，分析语义保持、近类歧义和远类反事实查询，从而区分可靠锚点与不稳定定位。再将推理蒸馏到学生模型，实现单图-查询对的统一定位与拒识。实验表明模型能拒绝缺失目标，同时提升存在目标的定位精度。
papers.abstract_en: Open-set visual grounding in remote sensing requires models to determine not only where a queried object is located, but also whether the image provides sufficient evidence for the query at all. Existing closed-set grounding models, however, tend to return plausible boxes even for absent objects, blurring localization confidence with genuine Visual Support. We introduce AnchorProbe-Distill (APD), a teacher-student framework that recasts open-set grounding as Visual Support learning. APD builds on the insight that supported queries should induce coherent spatial anchors, whereas unsupported or mismatched queries tend to produce unstable or misleading localization patterns. APD-T therefore uses the Original Query as a Reference Anchor to interpret query perturbations: Semantic-Preserving Queries retain the annotated target, Near-Category Ambiguous Queries are resolved according to whether they form a reliable alternative anchor or collapse onto the Reference Anchor, and Far-Category Counterfactual Queries provide rejection supervision. This reference-aware reasoning is distilled into APD-S, enabling unified localization and rejection from a single image--query pair. Experiments show that APD enables the resulting model to reject absent targets while also improving its localization of present targets.

papers.title_en: ActiveLang: Active Open-Vocabulary 3D Mapping with Semantic-Uncertainty-Guided Exploration
papers.authors: Liyan Chen, Hairong Yin, Huangying Zhan, Yi Xu, Raymond A. Yeh, Philippos Mordohai
papers.evidence: 面向语言标注开放词汇三维建图的自主机器人系统
papers.tldr: 面向未知环境中机器人需同时理解几何与开放语义的需求，ActiveLang 提出语义不确定性引导的主动开放词汇3D建图系统。它在紧凑双高斯表示上进行在线语言特征适配，联合重建几何、外观与开放词汇语义，并由规划器高效选择信息量大的视角。在 Replica 与 ScanNet++ 上，其2D/3D开放词汇分割显著优于在线和离线基线。结果表明主动探索能以更少观测和更低计算成本构建语言标注3D地图。
papers.abstract_en: As robots increasingly assist humans with diverse tasks, they need both geometric and semantic understanding of their surroundings. Moreover, robots often operate in unfamiliar environments and take on new tasks without knowing the relevant concepts ahead of time. This motivates language-annotated 3D maps that support open-vocabulary scene understanding and human-robot interaction. We introduce ActiveLang, an autonomous system for active open-vocabulary 3D mapping with semantic-uncertainty-guided exploration. ActiveLang performs online language-feature adaptation on a compact dual-Gaussian representation to jointly reconstruct scene geometry, appearance, and open-vocabulary semantics with modest memory overhead. Its planner efficiently selects informative viewpoints, enabling effective mapping with fewer observations and lower computational cost. Experiments on Replica and ScanNet++ demonstrate substantial improvements in 2D and 3D open-vocabulary segmentation over both online and offline baselines, highlighting that actively exploring scenes builds language-annotated 3D maps more efficiently.

papers.title_en: GeoFitBench-LLM: A Benchmark for Assessing Large Language Models' Capabilities in Geospatial Data Requirements Elicitation for Geo-Analytic Tasks
papers.authors: Amirhossein Vahdat, Thierry Badard, Luc Lamontagne
papers.evidence: 评估大模型推断地理空间数据需求的基准
papers.tldr: 大语言模型正成为GeoAI核心，但其地理空间数据需求获取能力缺乏评估，而检索型地理分析任务须先确定所需数据集与约束。GeoFitBench-LLM围绕时空关系推理与语义锚定两个维度，以固定且与提供方无关的schema编码真实需求，评估资源识别和属性级规格。七模型最小提示实验显示，资源识别常可实现，GPT-5.4 Thinking在66.67%请求中恢复完整资源集，但适用性规格仍随推理需求增加而变难。该工作为可复现评测LLM地理数据需求获取提供了基准。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models are becoming central to GeoAI systems, yet their evaluation rarely considers the elicitation of geospatial data requirements. This omission is critical as retrieval oriented geo-analytic tasks cannot be supported reliably without first identifying the necessary datasets and constraints. GeoFitBench-LLM is introduced as a benchmark for assessing whether LLMs can infer the datasets, the supporting resources and the constraints required by geo-analytic requests in natural language. The benchmark is structured around two reasoning dimensions, Spatio-Temporal Relational and Semantic Grounding, reflecting long-standing challenges in geospatial information retrieval and related natural language tasks. Ground truth requirements are encoded in a fixed, provider-independent schema for reproducible evaluation of resource identification and attribute-level specification. Experiments on seven models under minimal prompting indicate that identifying the necessary resources is often achievable, with GPT-5.4 Thinking achieving the best result by recovering the complete set of resources in 66.67% of benchmark requests. Results further indicate that accurate fitness-for-use specification remains more difficult as inferential demands increase.

papers.title_en: Benchmarking Answer-Grounding Consistency in Remote Sensing Visual Question Answering
papers.authors: Ping Guo, Zhiqi Huang, Xinran Li, Linkun Yu, Jingyin Pei, Kamata Seiichiro
papers.evidence: 融合遥感影像与文本并评估定位证据的视觉问答
papers.tldr: 遥感视觉问答中，模型既要给出文本答案，也要定位图像证据，但现有评测只看答案正确性或定位质量，忽略两者是否一致。为此，作者提出答案-证据支持协议AESP，按存在、计数、比较三类问题制定规则，检验定位证据能否支持模型自己的答案。同时构建G-RSVQA基准，含15027个样本及完整对象级标注。在七个接地视觉语言模型上，三类问题均出现证据支持失败，最高50.82%的正确答案不被其定位证据支持。
papers.abstract_en: In grounded remote sensing visual question answering, a model produces a textual answer and identifies relevant objects in the image as grounding evidence. Existing evaluations measure answer correctness and localization quality, but do not directly assess answer-grounding consistency. We propose the Answer-Evidence Support Protocol (AESP) to assess this consistency through evidence support: whether the grounding evidence supports the model's own answer. AESP applies task-specific rules to existence, counting, and comparison questions. We further construct the Grounded Remote Sensing Visual Question Answering (G-RSVQA) benchmark, containing 15,027 samples with questions, reference answers, and all related object-level annotations. Experiments on seven grounded vision--language models reveal failures of evidence support across all three question types. Up to 50.82% of correct answers in the evidence evaluation subset are not supported by the provided grounding evidence.
